_meta.description: Manually curated factor values per ISO-2 country. Top-level keys are factor IDs; values map ISO-2 → { value, year, source, url, note? }. Anything not in here is filled by fetch scripts (or rendered as 'no data' in the UI).

_meta.factor: Total data centre electricity demand forecast for ~2027 (TWh).
_meta.default_source: IEA Electricity 2024 — DC/AI/crypto demand category (2026 forecast), extrapolated to 2027 using the report's reported growth trajectory. National scaling cross-checked against JLL EMEA Data Centres Q4 2024 and Cushman & Wakefield Global Data Center Market Comparison 2024. Numbers are analyst-derived estimates; replace with vendor-licensed forecasts where available.

IE.source: IEA Electricity 2024, p32: 5.3 TWh (2022) doubling by 2026 → ~10.6 TWh (2026); ~11 TWh mid-2027 trajectory
IE.note: 2026 figure directly published by IEA (10.6 TWh); 2027 = mid-trajectory projection.

GB.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: UK DC share = 4% of national demand (2024). 2024 baseline ~10.6 TWh; extrapolated to 2027 using Ember's stated +30% by 2030 trajectory.
GB.note: Primary source cites % share, not absolute TWh; 2027 derived from 2024 baseline + 2030 trajectory.

DE.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Germany DC share = 4% (2024). 2024 baseline ~19 TWh; extrapolated to 2027.
DE.note: Primary cites 4% national share; 2027 derived from trajectory.

NL.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Netherlands DC share = 7% (2024). 2024 baseline ~8 TWh; grid effectively banning new DCs until 2030.
NL.note: Primary cites 7% share + grid moratorium; 2027 = limited growth above 2024.

FR.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: France DC share = 2% (2024). 2024 baseline ~9 TWh; France expected to maintain continued investment (less grid-constrained than NL/IE/DE-Frankfurt).
FR.note: Primary cites 2% share + grid investment continuing; 2027 derived.

DK.source: IEA Electricity 2024, p33: 6 TWh by 2026 (~20% of national demand)
DK.note: 2026 figure directly published by IEA (6 TWh); 2027 = mid-trajectory.

SE.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Sweden/Norway/Denmark expected to TRIPLE DC demand by 2030 from 2024 baseline.

NO.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Statnett plans tripling of DC demand by 2030 vs 2022 (~7 TWh implied 2022 baseline → 21 TWh by 2030); up to 15 TWh by 2050.
NO.note: Primary directly cites Statnett 3× by 2030 plan + 15 TWh by 2050; 2027 = early-trajectory.

FI.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Finland expected to see DC consumption 3-5× by 2035 from 2024 baseline; rapid growth.

ES.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: not in top-5 markets, growth expected; no explicit per-country TWh published.
ES.note: No primary per-country figure; estimate from Madrid pipeline activity (JLL EMEA H2 2024).

IT.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Italy expected 3-5× growth by 2035; one of named emerging markets.
IT.note: Primary cites 3-5× by 2035; no 2027 TWh published. Estimate from Milan pipeline.

PL.source: Ember 'Grids for data centres in Europe' 2025: Poland not in top-5; growth expected but no per-country TWh published.
PL.note: No primary per-country figure; estimate from Warsaw pipeline.

AE.source: C&W Global DC Market 2024 — Dubai + Abu Dhabi combined live + planned capacity converted to demand at ~70% utilisation. No per-country TWh published in IEA/Ember.
AE.note: Derived from C&W published MW figures + utilisation assumption; no primary TWh source.

SA.source: C&W Global DC Market 2024 — Riyadh hyperscale pipeline converted to demand. No per-country TWh published in IEA/Ember.
SA.note: Derived from C&W published MW + utilisation; no primary TWh source.

IL.source: C&W Global DC Market 2024 — Tel Aviv cluster; no per-country TWh published in IEA/Ember.
IL.note: Derived from C&W published MW; no primary TWh source.

_meta.factor: Typical end-to-end wait in years from a new >50 MW grid-connection application to energisation. Sourced from each national TSO's most recent published connection queue statistics (2024). Where a single number is misleading because of regional variation, the median across primary load centres is used.

GB.source: NESO TEC Register — average wait for transmission-connected demand >50 MW

IE.source: EirGrid 'Shaping our Electricity Future' — DC connection moratorium in Dublin region

NL.source: TenneT NL congestion map — 'transportbeperking' across Randstad
NL.note: Most of NL is currently congestion-restricted; new large loads queued behind grid reinforcements.

FR.source: RTE 'Schéma décennal de développement du réseau' 2024

ES.source: REE 'Planificación de la red de transporte 2021-2026'

AE.source: EWEC / DEWA / TAQA — hyperscale DC connection precedents 2023-2024

SA.source: Saudi Electricity Company — SAR 472 bn ($126 bn) 2024-2030 T&D capex programme implies fast-track industrial connections; MEED reporting
SA.note: URL repointed from se.com.sa (returns HTTP 500) to MEED coverage of SEC capex disclosure.

_meta.factor: Total forecast or committed transmission + distribution grid investment through 2030 (USD billion). Sourced from each national TSO's published 10-year network development plan (TYNDP for EU; equivalent national plans elsewhere). Converted to USD at end-2024 spot rate. Where the published plan extends beyond 2030 (e.g. 2045) the figure is pro-rated linearly.

GB.source: Ofgem RIIO-3 Final Determinations (Dec 2025): £28.1 bn upfront + £90 bn total investment pipeline by 2031, across gas + electricity transmission and distribution.
GB.note: £90 bn directly published by Ofgem press release Dec 2025; converted at 1.0 USD/GBP for rounded headline.

DE.source: BNetzA NEP 2037/2045 — EUR 283-300 bn by 2037 / 360-390 bn by 2045. Pro-rated to 2030 segment (~6 of 20 years) ≈ EUR 90-100 bn.
DE.note: NEP full-horizon figures directly cited; 2030-segment is pro-rata derivation.

FR.source: RTE 'Schéma décennal de développement du réseau' (SDDR) 2024 — EUR 100 bn transmission grid investment 2025-2040 directly published.
FR.note: EUR 100 bn 2025-2040 RTE transmission directly published; full-horizon figure (not pro-rated to 2030 — interpret accordingly).

IT.source: Terna 'Piano di Sviluppo 2025-2034' — EUR 23 bn (~USD 25 bn) total transmission investment over 10 years. Headline figure directly published March 2025.
IT.note: EUR 23 bn over 2025-2034 transmission-only headline confirmed by Terna press release Mar 2025.

ES.source: REE/Redeia — EUR 13.6 bn Spanish transmission grid investment 2025-2030 per Spanish government Network Development Plan 2025-2030.
ES.note: EUR 13.6 bn 2025-2030 transmission directly cited by Spanish gov NDP; converted to USD.

NL.source: TenneT — EUR 10 bn in 2024 alone, ~EUR 200 bn agenda over next decade (NL + DE combined). NL-only share + DSO (Stedin/Liander/Enexis) ~ EUR 85 bn to 2030.
NL.note: TenneT 2024 figure directly published; NL-only + DSO composite derivation.

IE.source: EirGrid Shaping Our Electricity Future + ESB Networks PR5

CH.source: Swissgrid Strategic Grid 2040 — CHF 5.5 bn (~USD 6 bn) total to 2040; ~CHF 3-4 bn (~USD 4 bn) to 2030 segment
CH.note: Corrected from prior $12 bn; Swissgrid Apr 2025 announcement confirms CHF 5.5 bn full programme value through 2040, of which the 2030 segment is ~70%.

SE.source: Svenska kraftnät — 1,500 km new + 2,500 km renewed transmission 2024-2033. Absolute SEK figure not published in headline; rough estimate based on typical SEK 10-15M/km build cost.
SE.note: Linear km published directly; SEK total is derivation from typical unit cost (NOT primary).

NO.source: Statnett — NOK 150 bn (~USD 14 bn) transmission grid investment over the next decade (2024-2033). Headline figure directly published.
NO.note: NOK 150 bn directly published in Statnett grid development plan.

DK.source: Energinet 'Sustainable transmission' — DKK 40 bn (~USD 6 bn) 2025-2028 transmission grid investment; pro-rated + DSO additions to ~USD 9 bn 2025-2030.
DK.note: DKK 40 bn 2025-2028 directly published; remainder is DSO addition extrapolated.

FI.source: Fingrid — EUR 400M/yr transmission investment 2024-2033 = EUR 4 bn (~USD 4.3 bn) decade-total. Headline directly published.
FI.note: EUR 400M/yr × 10yr trajectory directly published in Fingrid network development plan.

AE.source: DEWA Strategy 2030 + EWEC + TAQA transmission capex

SA.source: Saudi Electricity Company — SAR 472 bn 2024-2030 T&D capex programme. MEED + Argaam reports confirm USD ~126 bn six-year infrastructure initiative.
SA.note: Multiple primary press confirmations: MEED 2024, Argaam 2024.

_meta.factor: Median fixed-broadband download speed (Gbps). Sourced from Ookla Speedtest Global Index (Q1 2024 monthly snapshot). Country-level medians across all consumer and business fixed connections.
National 2030 broadband policy target (Gbps headline objective, not analyst median forecast). Sourced from each country's published gigabit / digital strategy plans. Treat as policy aspiration.

GB.source: UK Project Gigabit (DSIT 2024): gigabit-capable broadband to 99% of UK premises by 2030. Analysys Mason FTTP rollout trajectories support 1 Gbps median by 2030.
GB.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

DE.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030. Implemented in Germany via BMDV Gigabitstrategie 2030.
DE.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

FR.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030. Implemented in France via Plan France Très Haut Débit.
FR.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

IT.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030. Implemented in Italy via Piano Italia 1 Giga (Italia Domani).
IT.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

ES.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030. Implemented in Spain via Plan España Digital.
ES.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

NL.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030 for 100% of EU households.
NL.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

IE.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme (Decision EU 2022/2481): 1 Gbps fixed coverage for 100% of households by 2030. Implemented in Ireland via National Broadband Plan.
IE.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

SE.source: EU Digital Decade Policy Programme: 1 Gbps target by 2030. Implemented in Sweden via PTS Bredbandsstrategi 2030.
SE.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

AE.source: UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority — Vision 2031 fibre rollout targets average download speeds >1.5 Gbps by 2030 (current median already 0.4 Gbps via Speedtest).
AE.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.

SA.source: Saudi CST National Digital Infrastructure Strategy — 1 Gbps household coverage by 2030 per Vision 2030 digital pillar.
SA.note: Headline 2030 target directly published in cited policy programme.
